_comment: Workflow #2: an eval run, expressed as actions — and the proof that the
engine is workflow-agnostic.
Nothing in runnerlib changed to make this file work. It is a different
shape of work entirely — no stories, no PRs, no stages, no GitHub, a body
that runs a python script and a node whose command is not `claude -p` —
and it runs on the same load_actions/tick path as
config/actions-pipeline.json, at the same time, over the same board.
tests/test_agnosticism.py is that claim, asserted.
One topic carries an eval run:
cadre/evals/eval:<fixture>  — the whole run. `command` target=eval opens
it; each step writes a `signal` naming the
stage it finished. As everywhere else, the
coupling is the board: run_fixture.py has
never heard of judge_spec.py.
The trigger event carries the run's paths (story_path, out, board) because
the `where` vocabulary is closed and the engine resolves no paths of its
own — an eval run says where its own world is.
Prototype scope (evals/PLAN-2026-09.md, re-cut 2026-09-08): judges are
plain ad-hoc scripts writing jsonl. There is no backend here on purpose.
Relative argv paths, like actions-pipeline.json's `python3 -m
runnerlib.gh_watch`, resolve against the daemon's cwd — the repo.

actions.name: eval-requested
actions._why: S0 of an eval run. A `command` on the evals topic is somebody asking for a fixture story to be built and judged; the body builds it. In the prototype the build is a replay of a stored artifact (run_fixture.py) — the engine path is what is being proved, not the inference. The artifact path comes back on stdout and rides the emitted signal, so the next action needs no filesystem convention.

actions.name: fixture-done-to-judge
actions._why: The fixture's artifact exists, so judge it. `spawn_node` — the same body type that spawns a pipeline stage — resolves eval-judge-spec out of the same registry and formats the same kind of command template. That the resolved command turns out to be a python script rather than an agent CLI is invisible from here, which is the whole point (runnerlib/seed_eval_nodes.py).

actions.name: judge-done-to-report
actions._why: A judged run is a thing a human reads, not a thing that fires more work — UNKNOWN counts as FAIL at the gate and a rejection is a question for the driver, not an automatic retry. The summary is the judge's own tally line (judge_spec.summary_line), which it put on the signal; the notify is for anything watching the board.
